sections.title: Form and flowers
sections.text: This catalogue entry is Primula veris, cowslip. It is a perennial rosette herb, usually 10–30 cm tall, with wrinkled leaves about 5–15 cm long. Leafless stalks carry clusters of 10–30 nodding yellow flowers with orange markings.

sections.title: Food and caution
sections.text: Kew reports that the flowers and leaves are eaten. Cowslip is sometimes confused with the common primrose, P. vulgaris: cowslip flowers hang in a cluster on a taller stalk, while primrose flowers are usually solitary.
